qualification.cpu: Intel Core i9-13900H, KVM: CPU 0 performance and CPU 12 efficient
qualification.matrix: 168 forms x 33 state/fault cases x 2 C routes x 2 compilers x O0/O2 on both core classes and SDKs
qualification.state: All GPRs, full usable segment caches, RFLAGS, original-PC restart frames, CR2, NMI and ordinary physical RAM; page-table A/D and unusable-cache normalization excluded
qualification.composition: Zero/live counts, DF, FS/GS, address32 entry normalization, early compare termination, operand/fetch/competing faults; native IRQ/NMI observed-boundary replay; guest PTE repair, IRETQ and retry; context replacement across partial budgets/backing stops
qualification.software_checks: Raw-prefix/device-form refusal, missing/invalid progress binding, changed instruction bytes, first/later physical backing stops and retained prior progress

retained_counterexamples: third: hardware fast-string interrupt eligibility can occur after more than one element; event producer now replays the observed architectural boundary
second: narrow paged address argument generated a bad source call; the ABI owner now zero-extends the address carrier
fourth: destination-first CMPS faults across all widths and both core types; fixed the shared CMPSD single-element path
fifth: expanded corpus collided with oracle return breakpoints at 0x1800/0x1801; relocated those forms without dropping cases
final/native/paged-p: pre-existing refusal test still classified REP MOVSQ as native-only; replaced with unbound REP INS and checked addr32 MOVSQ remains distinct from ordinary source
admission-native/r6: ordinary canonical addr64 MOVS was already owned; narrowed the boundary regression to the newly admitted addr32 form

specifications.title: Intel SDM revision 093, volume 2 REP/string instructions, volume 3 exceptions and interrupt inhibition

limitations: Long-mode explicit paged binding only; ordinary undefined-effect proof coverage is not promoted
Elementwise producer-owned event boundaries do not predict physical fast-string grouping or asynchronous arrival timing
Explicit local processor profiles bind LODS count-high normalization and destination-first CMPS reads; other CPU families remain unqualified
Port-string effects, legacy i386 segmentation/task gates, gather/scatter/XSAVE progress and full software SMM/SGX/AEX remain open
TF, APIC/devices, MMIO/TLB/concurrent writers, LOCK and CET/FRED/LAM/LASS remain outside this paged binding
Existing IRET #AC VMX/NMI differences remain separately counted
No final LLVM release, SDK pin or LLVM gitlink update

post_integration.scope: Shared HighC return-tail performance change; REP feature sources unchanged. Rebuilt and requalified the affected REP exports after merging current dev; primary broader runs remain attached to their earlier implementation commit.
